title.value: The Primacy Bias in Deep Reinforcement Learning
title.justification: The title is mentioned multiple times in the provided text, often indicating the central focus of the research.
title.quote: The Primacy Bias in Deep Reinforcement Learning

analysis.description: This paper explores the primacy bias in deep reinforcement learning, where algorithms overfit to early experiences, affecting later learning. It proposes resetting parts of neural networks to mitigate this bias, improving performance in both discrete and continuous action domains.

type.justification: The paper conducts various experiments to demonstrate the primacy bias and test the effectiveness of the proposed resetting mechanism.
type.quote: Despite its simplicity, this resetting mechanism consistently improves performance of agents on benchmarks including the discrete-action ALE (Bellemare et al., 2013) and the continuous-action DeepMind Control Suite (Tassa et al., 2020).

name.justification: The paper centers on the concepts and challenges within deep reinforcement learning, specifically addressing biases in learning processes.
name.quote: This work identifies a common flaw of deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms: a tendency to rely on early interactions and ignore useful evidence encountered later.

name.justification: The study of biases and network resetting pertains broadly to techniques in deep learning.
name.quote: This work identifies a common flaw of deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms: a tendency to rely on early interactions and ignore useful evidence encountered later.

name.justification: The resetting of neural network layers is a core aspect of the proposed solution in the research.
name.quote: Our strategy is simple and compatible with any deep RL algorithm equipped with a replay buffer: we periodically re-initialize the last layers of an agent’s neural networks, while maintaining the experience within the buffer.

name.justification: The primacy bias concept is inspired by cognitive science, indicating an interdisciplinary approach.
name.quote: Inspired by cognitive science, we refer to this effect as the primacy bias.

name.justification: Soft Actor-Critic is explicitly used in the experiments discussed in the paper.
name.quote: To uncover in an explicit way the effect of the primacy bias in RL, we probe excessive reliance to early data to its extreme: could overfitting on a single batch of early data be enough to entirely disrupt an agent’s learning process? To investigate this question, we train Soft Actor-Critic (Haarnoja et al., 2018) on the quadruped-run environment from DeepMind Control suite (DMC) (Tassa et al., 2020).
